text: La Capilla is a town and municipality located in the Eastern Boyacá Province within the Colombian department of Boyacá. Its urban centre lies at an altitude of 1,600 metres (5,200 ft) in the Tenza Valley. The area was originally named La Capilla de Tenza due to the appearance of Our Lady of Candle in the outskirts of the village, which led to the construction of a chapel and the adoption of the name Capilla. The first inhabitants were the Muisca, part of the loose Muisca Confederation, and they were aligned with the caciques of Garagoa, Sutatenza, and Somondoco in the Tenza Valley. Conquistador Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada and his forces passed through the valley in 1537 en route to the territories of the zaque of Hunza. Modern La Capilla was officially established on November 13, 1793, by Juan de la Cruz Aguirre. The primary economic activity in La Capilla is agriculture, specifically the cultivation of cucumbers, tomatoes, and beans.
